'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Islamic terrorism]]
**Eighteen leaders of [[Jemaah Islamiyah]] announce the disbanding of the group, after 31 years of operation. The group committed several [[massacre]]s in [[Indonesia]], including the [[2002 Bali bombings|2002]] and [[2005 Bali bombings]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/4/southeast-asia-armed-group-jemaah-islamiyah-to-disband-report (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**[[Hezbollah]] launches at least 200 rockets and a swarm of [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]] at Israeli territory and threatens to expand its targeting range, in retaliation for the killing of Mohammed Nasser, a top Hezbollah commander. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/lebanons-hezbollah-says-it-launched-rockets-drones-israeli-military-sites-2024-07-04/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli occupation of the West Bank]]
**[[Israel]] approves the [[home construction|construction]] of 5,295 [[Israeli settlement|settler]] homes in dozens of settlements in the [[West Bank]], which are [[International law and Israeli settlements|internationally recognized as violating international law]]. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-hamas-war-news-07-04-2024-972cc86ab554103bba449dc117bee0d1 (AP)]
*[[Ituri conflict]]
**Six [[Chinese people|Chinese]] [[gold miner]]s and two [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese soldiers]] are killed during [[2021–2024 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks|an attack]] against a gold [[Mining industry of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|mine]] in [[Ituri Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. Two other workers are [[kidnap]]ped. [[CODECO]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://apnews.com/article/china-congo-mining-rebels-16bb24c828993da8a57b3621c30d0da5 (AP)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**The [[Islamic State]] kills eight people, including two [[civilian]]s, in an [[ambush]] on pro-[[Government of Syria|government]] [[militia]]men in [[Syria]]'s [[Syrian Desert|Badiya desert]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2024/07/04/isis-extremists-kill-eight-in-syria-desert-monitor- (Al Arabiya)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Hudson's Bay Company]], the parent company of [[Saks Fifth Avenue]], completes a merger and purchases luxury [[department store]]s [[Neiman Marcus]] and [[Bergdorf Goodman]] for [[United States dollar|$]]2.65 billion. [https://www.npr.org/2024/07/04/nx-s1-5028550/saks-buys-neiman-marcus-amazon-luxury-department-stores (NPR)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Hurricane Beryl]]
**Hurricane Beryl causes a six- to nine-feet high [[storm surge]] and fierce winds along [[Jamaica]]'s southern coast, killing at least one person before tracking towards the [[Cayman Islands]]. [https://www.cnn.com/weather/live-news/hurricane-beryl-storm-07-04-24/index.html (CNN)]
*Twenty-five people drown in southeast [[Sudan]] while trying to flee fighting between the [[Sudanese army]] and the [[Rapid Support Forces]]. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/world/africa/25-people-drown-in-sudans-blue-nile-river-fleeing-fighting-report (''Khaleej Times'')]
*Three people are killed and seven others are injured when a [[pickup truck]] is driven into a crowd celebrating [[Independence Day (United States)|Independence Day]] in the [[Lower East Side]] of [[Manhattan]] in [[New York City]], [[United States]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/suspected-impaired-driver-kills-three-new-york-city-park-2024-07-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*Eleven people die and another 153 people are diagnosed with [[West Nile fever]] in an ongoing outbreak in Israel. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/11-die-from-west-nile-fever-in-israel/3265804 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Germany–Turkey relations]]
**[[Germany]] summons [[Turkey]]'s [[ambassador]] to Germany in a [[Reciprocity (international relations)|tit-for-tat]] move over [[association football|footballer]] [[Merih Demiral]]'s [[wolf salute]] gesture while celebrating a goal at a [[UEFA Euro 2024]] match in [[Leipzig]], Germany, on Tuesday. [https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/04/sport/merih-demiral-celebration-controversy-turkey-euro-2024-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Shanghai Cooperation Organization]] officially grants membership to [[Belarus]]. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/belarus-joins-chinese-russian-shanghai-090745230.html (Yahoo! News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Violent incidents in reaction to the Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Antisemitism during the Israel–Hamas war]]
***[[Government of Greece|Greek]] [[Special Suppressive Antiterrorist Unit (Greece)|anti-terrorism police]] arrest seven people over [[arson]] attacks against an Israeli-owned hotel and a [[synagogue]] in central [[Athens]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/greece-arrests-7-over-arson-attacks-synagogue-israeli-owned-hotel-2024-07-04/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mass shootings in the United States]]
**Thirty-three people are killed in mass shootings at [[Independence Day (United States)|Fourth of July]] celebrations, with 11 people killed and 55 others injured in [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]], two people killed and three others injured in [[Huntington Beach, California]], one person killed and six others injured in [[Philadelphia]], [[Pennsylvania]], and one person killed and five others injured in [[Boston]], [[Massachusetts]]. [https://apnews.com/article/gun-violence-shootings-july-fourth-90bd7b9473e280e14429489decafd552 (AP)]
*[[2022 Oslo shooting]]
**[[Oslo District Court]] finds [[Iran|Iranian]]-born [[Norwegians|Norwegian]] Zaniar Matapour guilty of a shooting during [[Pride parade|pride celebrations]] in the [[Norway|Norwegian]] [[Oslo|capital]] in 2022 and [[sentence (law)|sentences]] Matapour to 30 years in prison. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/iran-norway-1.7254018 (CBC News)]
*[[M23 movement]]
**The [[Butembo]] [[military court]] in [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], sentences 25 [[FARDC]] soldiers to death for allegedly fleeing fighting against [[M23 rebels]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/4/dr-congo-sentences-25-soldiers-to-death-military (Al Jazeera)]
*Belarus frees ten [[political prisoner]]s including former opposition leader [[Ryhor Kastusioŭ]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/belarus-frees-10-political-prisoners-1400-remain-rights-group-says-2024-07-04/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Peruvian Congress]] votes 15–12 to pass a law introducing a statute of limitations on prosecuting [[crimes against humanity]] committed before July 2002. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/perus-congress-approves-statute-limitations-crimes-humanity-committed-111680838 (ABC News)]
*[[French people|French]] [[film director]] [[Benoît Jacquot]] is [[criminal charge|charged]] with the [[Rape in France|rape]]s of actresses [[Julia Roy]] and [[Isild Le Besco]] between 1998 and 2000, and "rape, [[sexual assault]] and violence" committed between 2013 and 2018. [https://apnews.com/article/metoo-france-movies-jacquot-godreche-af587b18cf58d16f35a00c7413759fc4 (AP)] [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/police-and-justice/article/2024/07/03/france-prosecutors-request-rape-charges-against-film-director_6676562_105.html (''Le Monde'')]
*[[Tunisia]]n opposition leader and founder of the [[Republican People's Union]] party Lotfi Mraïhi is arrested on suspicion of [[money laundering]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/4/tunisia-opposition-leader-lotfi-mraihi-arrested (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 United Kingdom general election]]
**Voters elect all 650 members of the [[United Kingdom]] [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]]. [[Keir Starmer]]'s [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] is projected to win a [[landslide victory]] according to [[exit poll]]s. [https://www.npr.org/2024/07/03/nx-s1-5026583/uk-election-2024-explained (NPR)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2024/07/04/uk-election-2024-live-updates-results/ (''The Washington Post'')]
**Former Labour leader [[Jeremy Corbyn]] is re-elected to the House of Commons as an independent [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MP]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/article/2024/jul/05/jeremy-corbyn-re-elected-in-islington-north-for-first-time-as-independent-mp (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Nigel Farage]], leader of the [[anti-immigration]] and [[Euroscepticism in the United Kingdom|Eurosceptic]] [[Reform UK]] party, is elected for the first time to a parliamentary seat representing [[Clacton (UK Parliament constituency)|Clacton]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/nigel-farage-wins-seat-uk-parliament-2024-07-05/ (Reuters)]
**Former Prime Minister [[Liz Truss]] loses her seat of [[South West Norfolk]], becoming the first former prime minister to lose their seat in over a century since [[Arthur Balfour]] in the [[1906 United Kingdom general election|1906 general election]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/liz-truss-general-election-norfolk-b2573293.html (''The Independent'')]
